messages:
miriam: Quick check — thinking about adding a span-merge window at ingest to reduce cardinality for lots of tiny RPCs (mobile heartbeat, short helpers). Wanted to surface tradeoffs before I proto something.

devon: Interesting. What's your target window length?

miriam: Starting idea was 200-300ms. Merge spans that share trace_id + parent_id and where start times are within window. We’d emit one synthetic span with aggregated duration/cost and a merged_count tag.

anish: Two quick concerns: 1) retries/hedging could get masked, 2) it can change how percentiles are computed downstream (you lose individual tail samples). :thinking_face:

sam: Also watch out for streaming/gRPC where a single logical operation emits many short spans that we actually want to see separately.

miriam: Agreed. Proposal to mitigate: only merge when span.name is in a whitelist (idempotent helpers), and attach merge_metadata so queries can opt-out. Example output: 
```
span.name: api.client.call
merged: true
merged_count: 4
merge_window_ms: 250
merge_reason: "short-idempotent"
```

katie: For cost attribution: are you planning to sum tokens/bytes across merged spans or average? If we over-assign cost to merged synthetic span we could distort billing dashboards.

miriam: Good point. My thought: store both raw_sum and smoothed_cost. smoothed_cost = min(raw_sum, decayed_baseline + burst_cap) — basically cap sudden spikes so a flood of tiny retries doesn't explode cost in a single minute. We keep raw_sum for auditability.

anish: Can you sketch heuristics? Even pseudo helps.

miriam: Sure — rough: 
```
if merge_condition: 
  raw_sum = sum(span.token_cost)
  smoothed = min(raw_sum, baseline + k * sqrt(raw_sum))
  emit {raw_sum, smoothed_cost: smoothed}
```

devon: OK but baseline needs to be per-route or per-tenant. Global baseline will punish small customers. Also we need to avoid exploding cardinality by keeping per-tenant baselines only when traffic > threshold.

miriam: Yes, per-tenant + per-route baseline. Threshold: 1req/s sustained for 1m to create a baseline. Otherwise use global fallback.

sam: How would this interact with existing sampling? If we sample 1/10 traces, merged counts still need to be upsampled, or else cost estimates will be wrong.

miriam: Plan: do merge before sampling so merge happens on all traces, then sampling keeps the merged metadata: merged_count and raw_sum. Billing pipeline will use raw_sum * sampling_inverse when available.

katie: I like keeping raw_sum. Suggest we also tag spans with merge_bucket (e.g., "short-helper-v1") so it's easy to filter in dashboards.

anish: Can we add a safety: never merge if span.duration > 1s or if it has an error tag. That keeps real tails observable.

miriam: Yep — safety rules: no-merge for errors, streaming flags, duration>1s, or explicit dont_merge span attribute.

devon: Ops impact: this will change ingest CPU but reduce downstream storage. We should run a canary in prod region for two weeks measuring: query fidelity (top-100 latency flows), storage delta, and billing delta.

miriam: Agreed. Action items: 
- miriam: prototype merge at the gateway (ingest) with whitelist + safety rules.
- devon: help define per-tenant baseline algorithm and thresholds.
- katie: validate billing pipeline can consume raw_sum + sampling factor.
- anish: write quick dashboard to compare counts/percentiles pre/post.

ops-bot: Note: created ticket INF-8092 prototype span-merge window (epic: obs-cost-optim).

sam: SGTM. One more ask — add a feature flag so we can toggle by customer or route.

miriam: Will do. I'll push a short RFC with examples and some sample queries tomorrow. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
